title: Runtimes
engine: knitr

A runtime is mutable state used while authoring a DAG or tracking execution.
Finalizing it creates an immutable DAG. Use the CLI to inspect and administer
open work; use named committed DAGs for completed research.

## Freeze and resume runtimes

```{bash}
runtime_ref="$(dml runtime create)"
printf '["scalar",42]\n' | dml runtime put-literal "$runtime_ref" - --name answer >/dev/null
frozen_ref="$(dml runtime freeze "$runtime_ref" --message "Review staged input")"

dml runtime list | jq -e --arg frozen "$frozen_ref" '.[] | select(.id == $frozen)'
dml runtime describe "$frozen_ref" | jq -e '.state == "frozen" and .frozen_message == "Review staged input"'
answer_ref="$(dml runtime get-node "$frozen_ref" answer)"
dml dag get-node "$answer_ref" | jq -e '.[1] == 42'

resumed_ref="$(dml runtime unfreeze "$frozen_ref")"
dml runtime freeze "$resumed_ref" --message "Leave the demonstration read-only" >/dev/null
```

Freezing preserves partial nodes, tags, and execution identity, but does not
create a result. Its message is a reason, not a durable name. `Dag.freeze()`
and `Dag.unfreeze()` manage the normal Python wrapper; `dml.resume(frozen,
name=..., message=...)` resumes it in another process. Runtime and execution
identities are complete `Ref` values (`index:` or `frozenindex:`), never bare
IDs.

### Move a checkpoint to another computer

Freeze before exporting. `dag.export_snapshot()` (or
`dml.runtime.export_snapshot(frozen_ref)`) returns versioned JSON containing the
frozen index and its complete local repository-object dependencies. Save that
string in durable storage before stopping the source computer.

```{python}
import daggerml as dml

draft = dml.new()
draft.put({"epoch": 2, "loss": 0.5}, name="checkpoint")
draft.freeze("handoff")
snapshot = draft.export_snapshot()

# An empty project models the replacement computer's local database.
with dml.temporary(remote_root=draft.dml.config.get("remote.root")) as replacement:
    resumed = dml.resume(snapshot=snapshot, dml=replacement)
    assert resumed["checkpoint"].value() == {"epoch": 2, "loss": 0.5}
    resumed.commit(resumed.put({"epoch": 3}))
```

`dml.resume()` and `dml.runtime.unfreeze()` accept exactly one local frozen ref
or `snapshot=` string. The destination must use the same `remote.root` and have
access to its execution records and referenced artifacts. Export is repeatable
and leaves the frozen runtime intact; successful resumption consumes its remote
activation claim. A second computer cannot activate another copy of that
checkpoint. Older checkpoints become stale after resumption, even if the same
execution is frozen again.

A newer checkpoint can return to a project that still holds an older frozen
copy of the same execution. Import reconciles that superseded copy and stale
activation staging after validating the remote checkpoint; it does not overwrite
a locally owned active generation or conflicting immutable graph objects.

Both user-authored and execution-aware function runtimes can be frozen. The
execution becomes `suspended`, not terminal; its identity, arguments, lineage,
cache pointer, and executor continuation remain in place. Resumption claims a
new runtime generation, and stale local indexes cannot publish results under an
old generation. Cancellation remains valid during suspension and prevents later
resumption. Retry the same freeze/unfreeze operation after an interrupted remote
response; locally staged state retains the generation needed to finish it.

Snapshots are application checkpoints, not Python stack or process images.
Continue explicitly from named checkpoint nodes and commit the ordinary result.
The original adapter is not relaunched or allowed to turn its old process's exit
into a failure of the resumed execution; its handles remain available for
cleanup/cancellation. Resumption does not move PIDs, containers, or external
side effects, and does not make local executor teardown portable. Quiesce the
old application at the checkpoint; graph fencing is not a sandbox for arbitrary
Python side effects. Do not share one mutable project database between competing
application writers.

Snapshot JSON contains repository data, not external artifact bytes, remote
execution records, or ambient credentials. Treat snapshots as trusted project data, not
authenticated authorization tokens. All repository dependencies must be local
when exporting; deepen shallow history first if required parent objects are
missing. Keep checkpoint files independently durable: remote graph collection
does not discover snapshots stored outside the repository.

## Inspect, cancel, and refresh deliberately

`runtime describe`, `describe-graph`, and `read-execution-record` report graph,
lifecycle, lineage, cancellation, invalidation, adapter continuation, shared
retry deadlines, and cleanup. Cleanup may remain pending or fail without making
an otherwise reusable result unavailable.

For script and local Docker, the launching effective user and hostname must
participate in polling, cleanup, and cancellation. Other users/hosts return retry without touching local
resources; there is no automatic takeover. A published result remains reusable
while owner-dependent cleanup is pending.

```{bash}
course_ref="$(dml show | jq -er '.dags["course-execution"]')"
first_ref="$(dml dag get-node-by-name "$course_ref" script-first)"
execution_dag_ref="$(dml dag describe-node "$first_ref" | jq -er '.dag')"
cache_key="$(dml dag describe "$execution_dag_ref" | jq -er '.cache_key')"
cache_description="$(dml cache describe "$cache_key")"
execution_ref="$(jq -er '.execution' <<< "$cache_description")"

jq -e --arg dag "$execution_dag_ref" '.dag == $dag and .lifecycle == "succeeded"' <<< "$cache_description"
printf '%s\n' "$execution_ref" > "$DOCS_WORKSPACE_ROOT/invalidated-course-execution"
dml cache invalidate "$execution_ref"
```

Rerunning the same stored runnable and argument produces a new execution for the
same normalized cache key:

```{python}
import daggerml as dml

course = dml.load("course-execution")
with dml.new("course-refresh", message="refresh invalidated course work") as dag:
    runnable = dag.put(course["script"], name="script")
    source = dag.put(course["source"], name="source")
    refreshed = runnable(source, name="refreshed")
    dag.commit(refreshed)

assert dml.load("course-refresh").result.value() == {"count": 3, "total": 10}
```

```{bash}
refreshed_ref="$(dml show | jq -er '.dags["course-refresh"]')"
refreshed_result="$(dml dag get-node-by-name "$refreshed_ref" refreshed)"
refreshed_dag="$(dml dag describe-node "$refreshed_result" | jq -er '.dag')"
refreshed_key="$(dml dag describe "$refreshed_dag" | jq -er '.cache_key')"
new_execution="$(dml cache describe "$refreshed_key" | jq -er '.execution')"
old_execution="$(cat "$DOCS_WORKSPACE_ROOT/invalidated-course-execution")"
test "$new_execution" != "$old_execution"
```

Invalidate exact execution refs, not cache keys or DAG refs. This affects every
caller sharing `remote.root`, so inspect the returned identity and coordinate
before refreshing work. Cancellation first selects the complete unreferenced
set as `cancel-pending`, conditionally removes matching cache pointers, then
cancels adapters concurrently. Retry responses share `not_before`; repeated
`dml runtime cancel index:... --max-retries 3` resumes pending cancellation.
An execution that already finished is a successful no-op. Continue with
[Sharing](sharing.qmd); cache invalidation is deliberately last among workflows
that need the original cached result.
